get.description:
Return the current ERC-20 allowance per (wallet, token, spender).

Derived from the latest indexed Approval event for each triple — this is
a read model over the append-only `onchain_event` log, not a separate
mutable table. `is_unlimited` flags allowances at or above
``_UNLIMITED_ALLOWANCE_THRESHOLD``, the standard "infinite approval"
security signal.

List assets with optional exclusion/held filters and cursor pagination.

`held` and `excluded` are independent filters — an excluded asset that is
still held by a wallet must remain reachable via held=true&excluded=true,
so it can be un-excluded from the UI.

post.description:
Add a manually tracked ERC-20 asset.

Returns the existing asset (409) if the contract_address is already tracked.

patch.description: Update an asset's exclusion state or decimals override.

get.description:
Serve a cached asset icon (AUD-385), or 404 if none is cached.

Only ever serves what `asset_icon_refresh` has already cached — this
route never fetches the upstream inline, so a cold cache 404s (the
frontend falls back to a generated monogram) instead of slowing down
the request.
Return cached news articles for *asset_id*, newest first.

Report the pinned catalog snapshot's source, version and coverage.

No catalog has necessarily been imported yet (the import runs as part of
discovery) — report zero coverage rather than erroring in that case.
Return counts of what WOULD be deleted by a purge without modifying data.

Return a paginated list of indexed on-chain Transfer events.

Results are ordered newest-first (block_number DESC, log_index DESC).
`raw_amount` stays the raw uint256 decimal-string source of truth.
`amount` / `value_usd` / `price_usd` are derived, human-readable
enrichment: `value_usd` and `price_usd` are the *latest known* price at
request time (the most recent `quote_set` with `status = 'complete'`),
not a historical price as of the event's block — this endpoint does not
do a price-at-block lookup, so callers must not present it as such.
Stream full history as JSON or CSV.  Optional ``from`` / ``to`` bound the date range.
Stream current portfolio as JSON or CSV.

Return portfolio value history for the requested period.

Entries are ordered newest-first.  Gap markers (is_gap_marker=true) are
synthetic entries inserted where the timeline has a discontinuity; they
have no snapshot_id and total_value_usd is null.

Use next_cursor to fetch the next page (null = exhausted).

Return constituent holdings lines for a specific historical snapshot.

Each line includes observation_id for exact balance provenance.  Lines are
ordered by value_usd descending (unknown values last).
Return job run history, newest first (keyset cursor pagination).

post.description:
Queue an immediate job run, coalescing if one is already queued or active.

Enqueues a ``pending`` row (AUD-313/AUD-318 pattern) instead of inserting an
``in_progress`` row directly — a run only starts once the worker actually
claims and dispatches it via :func:`claim_pending_job`, so the ID returned
here is always a real, eventually-executed run rather than a zombie the
worker will never pick up.

``wallet_id`` scopes ``balances``/``discovery`` requests to a single wallet
(AUD-399/AUD-400) — the wallet-card "Refresh balances" / "Discover tokens"
actions, so a single address can be refreshed without re-scanning every
tracked wallet. Coalescing is scope-aware: a global request never swallows
a per-wallet one and vice versa, and two requests for different wallets
never coalesce onto each other.

get.description: Return a single job run by ID, or 404.

post.description:
Cancel a pending or in-progress job.

Returns 404 if the job does not exist or is already in a terminal state.
